records.name: AlbertPowerAssoc.jpow_mul_jpow
records.doc:
A sequential product on the effects of an order-unit space is a binary operation a & b, read "first test a, then test b with the state updated by the first test", satisfying the seven axioms S1-S7 of van de Wetering (arXiv:1803.11139, Definition 2). This development registers two classification theorems for such products on the Hermitian matrix algebras.
On H_N(R), the Hermitian N x N real matrices with N >= 1, every sequential product is the Lueders product sqrt(a) b sqrt(a): there is no free parameter. On H_N(C) with N >= 3, every sequential product has the twist normal form a^(1/2+it) b a^(1/2-it) for a unique real t. The twist family is a one-parameter deformation of the Lueders product, and the complex theorem says nothing outside it satisfies the axioms.
Prior art. That Lueders is not the only sequential product, and twisted products of this shape in particular, are not new: Gudder asked the question in 2005, Shen and Wu answered it negatively and gave a general construction in 2009 (arXiv:0905.0596), and Liu, Wu and Wu showed those examples are unitary equivalent to Lueders (arXiv:1009.2593). What is registered here is the converse direction. The examples are not exhibited; they are shown to be forced, with the parameter unique, and with no product outside the family admissible. The equations are asserted on all effects, including singular ones, and the uniqueness of t is part of the registered statement.
Direction. Both registered classification theorems are necessity: a product satisfying the axioms is supplied, and the theorem says it has the stated normal form. The two converses differ in status and neither is registered. For the complex case, that each real t defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is proved in the wider development; together with the registered uniqueness it is what would make the parameter map injective. For the real case, that the Lueders formula defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is not proved anywhere in this development. Nothing here registers a bijection between parameters and products, or the admissibility of the Lueders formula.
The package also registers two classical theorems the development proves in passing. Albert's power-associativity theorem: in a commutative Jordan ring carrying an R-module structure, x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed. And the real case of Wigner's theorem: every transition probability preserving self-map of the rays of a finite-dimensional real inner product space is induced by a linear isometry, with bijectivity not assumed but derived.
Both classification theorems are proved from S1-S7 with no hypotheses beyond the dimension bounds, and their axiom closures contain only Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The continuity axiom S2 is stated in the order-unit norm, as an explicit epsilon-delta condition, so the statement file depends on no normed-space or topological instance; the equivalence with continuity in the carrier's Frobenius topology is proved in the development.
Scope. The repository carries three Comparator configurations, selecting four theorems between them: the two sequential-product classifications above, which use the SeqProd interface and the axiom S2 and correspond to numbered rows of the manuscript; and the two ancillary classical theorems, Albert and Wigner, which use neither and correspond to no manuscript row. Each configuration is a separate submission and a separate entry; no one entry contains all four. No Palomar claim is made here for any other declaration in the repository.
The two classification theorems are two rows of a thirty-six row manifest tracking the numbered results of the accompanying manuscript. The manuscript as a whole is not formalized: as of 2026-08-12 the manifest stands at 12 rows formalized, 19 partial, and 5 absent. In particular the quaternionic row H_n(H) and the Albert-algebra row H_3(O) of the manuscript's main theorem are not proved here, and the coalescence and diagonal-homomorphism lemmas are established on the concrete carrier H_N(C) rather than at the manuscript's stated generality of a finite-dimensional simple Euclidean Jordan algebra.

records.name: PalomarCubicHalfSpectrum.released_outer_source_normal_form

records.name: ZetaLean.PalomarDH.dh_analytic_half
records.doc: Davenport and Heilbronn (1936) exhibited a Dirichlet series with real coefficients satisfying a Riemann-type functional equation which nevertheless has zeros off the critical line. It is the standard demonstration that a functional equation of Riemann type does not on its own force the Riemann Hypothesis, it is the reference counterexample against which structural explanations of the Riemann Hypothesis are tested, and the location of its zeros remains an active subject. The function is DH(s) = (1 - i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi) + (1 + i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi^-1) for a quartic Dirichlet character chi mod 5 and kappa = (sqrt(10 - 2*sqrt 5) - 2)/(sqrt 5 - 1), the value that rotates the two conjugate root numbers onto each other and so makes the Dirichlet coefficients real. This submission advertises one theorem, the analytic half of the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: there exists an entire function represented by the Davenport-Heilbronn Dirichlet series on Re z > 1 whose completion (pi/5)^(-(s+1)/2) * Gamma((s+1)/2) * f(s) is symmetric under s -> 1-s. The statement is existential in f, so it carries its own non-vacuity and needs none of the character theory used to construct the witness. What the work consists of. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is not a library object anywhere we could find, so the development builds it: the quartic character mod 5, the linear combination, entirety on all of C, the identification of the Dirichlet coefficients as the real period-5 sequence 1, kappa, -kappa, -1, 0, and the completed functional equation. The last of these is where the content sits. It reduces to a root-number identity whose convention-sensitive constants are derived inside the development, from Mathlib's Real.cos_pi_div_five by radical algebra, rather than transcribed from a table; the standard sources state kappa without deriving it in a form a kernel will accept, and getting it wrong yields a function whose coefficients are not real and which therefore is not the counterexample. The functional equation is stated with explicit guards excluding the poles of the two Gamma factors, because Mathlib's junk value Gamma = 0 at the poles would otherwise make the unrestricted equation false for reasons having nothing to do with the mathematics. Audience. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is a named object of analytic number theory with a continuing literature on its zeros, so a machine-checked construction of it is of direct interest to number theorists working on zeros of L-functions and on what a Riemann-type functional equation does and does not imply. It is also the object a formalized treatment of the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem has to have before it can say anything, and this supplies it in a form that carries its own non-vacuity. Prior art. A search of Mathlib at the revision pinned by this repository found no Davenport-Heilbronn function and no formalization of this functional equation. That is a bounded search of one library. No systematic search of other proof assistants or of the mathematical literature for prior formalizations has been run, and no novelty against the literature is claimed: the mathematics is Davenport and Heilbronn's, published in 1936. Scope. The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem itself is NOT proved here. Its full statement additionally requires a zero s with Re s different from 1/2, and that conjunct appears nowhere in the advertised theorem. What is offered is the analytic half alone. No numerical enclosure for any zero of DH is asserted, and nothing here is a statement about the Riemann zeta function or the Riemann Hypothesis.

records.name: Palomar.Erdos730.erdos_730_infinite
records.doc: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs of solved research problems from the Erdős problems collection, hosted as stable formal_proof targets for Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures. The principal result is an affirmative answer to Erdős Problem #730 (Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa and Straus, 1975): the set of pairs n < m for which binom(2n, n) and binom(2m, m) have the same set of prime divisors is infinite, and in fact contains infinitely many consecutive pairs (n, n + 1). The proof formalises the argument posted informally by Liam Price on the problem's discussion page on 24 June 2026: Kummer's theorem converts equality of prime supports into a base-p digit condition, an explicit quadratic family of consecutive pairs is constructed, a fixed-depth Fourier estimate bounds the digit obstruction on blocks of length p^r, a uniform depth tail uses a Mertens-type reciprocal-prime input, the top-prime range is handled by fixed-modulus divisor switching using the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions, and an exact rational density budget yields positive lower density and hence infinitude. The repository also proves the sumset form of Erdős Problem #154 (equidistribution of A + A in residue classes for Sidon sets A with |A| ~ sqrt N, from Lindström's theorem) and hosts smaller bounded results for Problems #94, #399 and #1074. Every tracked theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; each registry statement under Palomar/ restates its result in a Challenge importing Mathlib alone.

records.name: PalomarKinnim.physicalApportionmentExactMinimum
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of all sixteen units of Mishnah Kinnim, with a machine-checked physical optimization theorem for the Koppel--Reiss reading of Kinnim 3:2. For any list of pair counts grouped by owner, the priest has already acted on exactly half of the mixed birds above and half below. A physical world records one action level for every individual bird of every owner. Lean proves that every such world is compatible, by permutation, with the fixed half-split action list. Counting valid birds directly from each owner's closed-pair quota, the theorem proves that the exact minimum over all physical apportionments is twice the complement of the largest attainable subset sum not exceeding half the total, and constructs an apportionment attaining it. The repository also covers all sixteen units, flight recurrences, and replacement-inventory covers.

records.name: KaltonPeck.rankParityGeneral
records.doc:
We prove the following mod-2 identity for real symplectic Banach spaces:
  If $(X, \omega)$ is a real symplectic Banach space, and $T \in L(X)$ satisfies:
    (1) $I + T^+T$ is Fredholm
    (2) $I + T^2$ has finite rank

records.name: PalomarQseriesPrimeCoefficients.BCoeff_not_multiplicative_witness
records.doc: For an explicitly defined difference B of two signed cone theta series over Q(sqrt(5)), Lean proves a closed nonmultiplicativity witness and a complete prime-index classification. For every rational prime p congruent to 1 modulo 10, B((p-1)/10) is one of -2, -1, 1, 2; a norm-negative golden integer generator and its strict fundamental-window normalization exist; and the coefficient has magnitude two exactly when the resulting geometric residue invariant is one modulo three. The invariant is also proved independent of the generator within the explicitly defined signed fundamental-unit orbit.

records.name: Palomar.fjp_1_1_isSheafy
records.doc:
A Lean 4 formalisation of *Uniform sheafy Tate rings that are not stably uniform* (Birkbeck–Torzewski), answering Question 7 of Kedlaya's *Nonarchimedean Scottish Book* in the negative: a sheafy uniform Huber pair need not be stably uniform. Buzzard–Verberkmoes and Mihara proved that stably uniform Tate Huber rings are sheafy; whether the converse holds was open.
The paper gives two complete Tate algebras over a complete discretely valued field `k` that are uniform, nonnoetherian integral domains with `A° = A₀`, strongly sheafy (every Tate algebra `A⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩` is sheafy), and yet not stably uniform, because an explicit rational localisation is not uniform. The first (Theorem 1.1) is the finite-jet pinching algebra `𝓐 = B ×_D C`, the pullback of a Milnor square with `B = k⟨W, Q⟩/(Q²)`, `C = k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩`, `D = C/(Q²)` — concretely, the series in `k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩` whose `Q⁰`- and `Q¹`-coefficients have nonnegative `W`-support; its bad chart `𝓐⟨W/ϖ⟩ ≅ k⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²)` is non-reduced. The second (Theorem 8.1) is the weighted-parity algebra `𝒜_w`, whose bad chart is an integral domain; the paper proves it for every unbounded weight `w ≥ 1`, the formalisation for `w(n) = n`.
This submission certifies the seven conclusions of Theorem 1.1 together with two statements ruling out a vacuous reading of its sheafiness claims, stated self-containedly on Mathlib in `Challenge.lean` over an arbitrary complete ultrametric field with DVR valuation ring; Theorem 8.1 is certified by the repository's in-library configuration. The repository also develops the surrounding theory after Wedhorn's *Adic Spaces*: Huber and Tate rings, the adic spectrum, rational localisations, the structure presheaf, and sheafiness (Definition 8.26), including the strongly noetherian theorem (8.28(b)).

records.name: MiscMath.Geometry.tendsto_log_coveringNumber_sphere_div_atTop
records.doc: For a fixed angular radius theta in (0, pi/2), the least number M(n, theta) of spherical caps of angular radius theta, centred at points of the unit sphere of R^n, whose union is that whole sphere satisfies (1/n) log M(n, theta) -> -log sin theta as n -> infinity. This is the covering half of Wyner (1967): the elementary volume bound gives the lower bound on the covering number and a random-covering argument gives the upper bound. The statement is given in Mathlib's own vocabulary, as an asymptotic for Metric.coveringNumber of Metric.sphere 0 1 in EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) at chordal radius 2 sin (theta/2), and introduces no definition of its own; two compared lemmas establish that an angular cap of half-angle theta about a unit vector is exactly the closed chordal ball of that radius, which is what licenses reading the result as a statement about caps. Two further compared theorems rule out the junk values that the N-infinity-valued covering number and the logarithm would otherwise admit.

records.name: SZ.sqrtTwo_mem_S
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which answers a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. records.name: SquareMaximalityPalomar.squareMaximality
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of square maximality for spanning trees of induced subgraphs of the square lattice. For every positive integer n and every finite set S of n^2 points in Z^2, the induced lattice graph on S has at most as many spanning trees as the n by n square, with equality exactly when S is a translate of that square. The development also proves the corresponding strict and equality statements for arbitrary spanning subgraphs, together with the finite Matrix--Tree theorem and the proof chain used by the paper.

records.name: SparseFock.MainTheorem.fully_independent_sparseStack_matrix
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of three sparse oblivious-subspace-embedding results at the Nelson--Nguyen parameter scale: the fully independent signed-hash SparseStack construction, independent uniform signed exact-s columns, and a limited-independence transfer for finite laws whose combined hash-sign selector marginals agree with SparseStack through order 4q.  At the stated rounded parameters the selected theorems give failure probability at most delta, with explicit strict bounds s < 1356 q / epsilon and m < 306456 (d + q) / epsilon^2 where those parameter conclusions are packaged. records.name: KoecherAlfsenShultz.orderIso_preservesJordan
records.doc:
A Euclidean Jordan algebra is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space carrying a commutative bilinear product with a unit, satisfying the Jordan identity (x*y)*(x*x) = x*(y*(x*x)) and the associativity of the inner product <x*y, z> = <y, x*z>. This is Faraut-Koranyi's definition (Analysis on Symmetric Cones, III.1). This development formalizes the classical structure theory of these algebras.
Mathlib carries the Jordan identity as the typeclass IsCommJordan together with five operator-commutation lemmas, and nothing beyond that: no idempotent theory, no Peirce decomposition, no spectral theory. This development supplies that layer.
The registered results, in four separate Comparator configurations. (1) The Koecher / Alfsen-Shultz theorem: a unital linear order isomorphism of a Euclidean Jordan algebra is a Jordan automorphism, with the cone taken to be the sums-of-squares cone and the product carried as a bundled bilinear map so that the statement needs no ring instance to elaborate. (2) The single-element spectral theorem: every element of a finite-dimensional formally real Jordan algebra is a real linear combination of a complete family of pairwise-orthogonal idempotents. Finite-dimensionality is load-bearing rather than decorative - the polynomial algebra R[X] satisfies every other hypothesis and has no nonconstant spectral resolution. (3) The Jordan trace form tau(x,y) = tr(L_{x*y}): symmetric, associative, and positive definite, constructed from the multiplication alone rather than assumed. records.name: Scott1980.Neighborhood.theorem_8_8
records.doc: A Lean 4 / mathlib formalization of Dana Scott's 1980 Oxford lectures, published May 1981 as PRG-19 Lectures on a Mathematical Theory of Computation. The principal sourced Palomar result is the first sentence of Theorem 8.8: the neighbourhood system U over [0,1) ⊆ ℚ is universal, in the sense that every countable neighbourhood system D embeds as a subdomain (D ⊴ U). Comparator also selects two new formal corollaries: P4_embeds for Scott's Example 1.5 and Ssys_embeds for Exercise 7.22. Scott defines those systems but does not separately state the embeddings. Challenge.lean fixes the neighbourhood-system vocabulary, including Scott's standing assumption that the master token set Δ is non-empty, Scott's ⊴, and the concrete Definition 8.7 family U. This foundational universality result supplies a concrete host for all countable domains; it is relevant to domain theory, denotational semantics, mathematical logic, and formalized mathematics. The broader Lectures I–VIII development lives in Scott1980/Neighborhood/* and is not the advertised Comparator result. The informal account is arxiv.md; the working transcription is sources/PRG19.md. Lean was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott did not participate in or endorse this formalization. records.name: PalomarQseriesRowFactorization.mk_factorization
records.doc: A Lean 4 verification of an explicit rank-two indefinite theta completion over Q(sqrt(5)). The registered results cover the coefficientwise row-model factorization; the exact holomorphic-sign-part bridge; summability of the defining completed-theta lattice series; a specialization of Zwegers' Lemma 2.8; the weight-one T and S transformations, including the five-to-two characteristic reduction; the exact mixed boundary derivative and Bruinier--Funke image; and a kernel-checked nonharmonicity witness.

The registered results cover the coefficientwise row-model factorization; the exact holomorphic-sign-part bridge; summability of the defining completed-theta lattice series; a specialization of Zwegers' Lemma 2.8; the weight-one T and S transformations, including the five-to-two characteristic reduction; the exact mixed boundary derivative and Bruinier--Funke image; and a kernel-checked nonharmonicity witness.

records.name: MeyerProblem.Palomar.shiftedSquareRootClassification
records.doc: For 0 < θ < 1, this Lean 4 formalization classifies tempered atomic measures whose support and Fourier support are contained in the shifted square-root set Λθ = {±√(n + θ) | n ∈ ℕ₀}. In an equivalent polynomial-growth coefficient model, it proves that the −1 and i Fourier eigenspaces vanish, identifies the surviving 1 and −i eigenspaces as one-dimensional lines generated by explicit generalized eta products up to the respective thresholds θ ≤ 1/8 and θ ≤ 3/8, and proves that the full admissible space has dimension 2, 1, or 0 in the resulting three θ ranges.

records.name: GCD369InvariantFibreDichotomy
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a two-sheet implication in the aligned nontrivial cubic-Kummer analysis at actual partial degrees (6,9). Every field-valued solution of the four lower-Pfaffian invariant equations is proved to lie on a common-power sheet with zero source bracket or on an elliptic sheet; converse inclusions and existence of the sheets are not compared.  The formalization derives the elliptic equation and terminal one-form, excludes nonconstant reduced rational trajectories on its C != 0 fibre by a finite forbidden-value argument, factors the C=0 fibre, and verifies the shifted Davenport--Stothers bracket and terminal descent. Version 2 derives the finite-place valuation classification directly from the reduced rational ODE, proves the one-point support theorem, and excludes that sheet in the noncube Kummer branch.  It does not claim the preceding landing from an arbitrary Keller pair, the cube branch, all (6,9), maximum eleven, or JC2.

records.name: Zeta23Ext.PalomarV2.n_point_bound
records.doc: Let N(T,2T) count the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with ordinate in (T,2T], with multiplicity, and N_0^s(T,2T) the simple zeros among them on the critical line. The Lean development accompanying arXiv:2608.13637 (anthropics/zeta-23-lean) proves, for Mathlib's riemannZeta and unconditionally, that for every eps > 0 and all large T, (H - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), with H = 3/2 - (1/sqrt 2) cot(1/sqrt 2) = 0.67250070367941164573... (its Theorem D). Ainta (github.com/ainta/zeta-simple-zeros) refines H by carrying the spectral defect of the Gram matrix of the simple-zero vectors through that argument and bounding it block by block through a local inequality on seven points. Advertised here: that refinement carried out for n points at once, and three instances. Parametrically, for n >= 2, c > 0, m >= n, p > 0 with c(m-(n-1)) <= 1, if c <= F(n,p,g) for every nonnegative vector g of n-1 gaps (the hypothesis hCert), then for every eps > 0 and all large T, (Phi_n(n,c,m,p) - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), where Phi_n(n,c,m,p) = (H - (n-1)(m-1)/(pm)) / (1 - c(m-(n-1))/m). At n = 7 this is Ainta's theorem. THE THREE-POINT INSTANCE IS UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (3, 1345/10^6, 3000) the hypothesis is proved, not assumed: the overlap weight w = k^2 is enclosed from a twelve-term Taylor bound on cos and sin and the closed form of the kernel, and 368 interval cell lemmas over rationals, applied 1515 times over 487 leaves, cover the quarter-plane of the two gaps. No external interval-arithmetic certificate is assumed for the three-point theorem, and no floating point appears. The cap gives m = 745 and the constant (149000000 H - 99200)/148800133 = 0.67273733450380945875..., exceeding H by 2.3663e-4: for Mathlib's riemannZeta, an unconditional improvement of the dependency's Theorem D. THE FOUR-POINT INSTANCE IS ALSO UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (4, 2310/10^6, 2500), the finite inequality at every triple of nonnegative gaps is proved inside Lean. The cap gives m = 435 and the resulting constant is (906250 H - 1085)/904171 = 0.67284701976668870316.... The bound and ratio carry no certificate hypothesis and use exactly the same three permitted axioms. The eight-point instance stays conditional. Our n-point generalisation of Ainta's interval verifier accepts c = 41763/10^7 at p = 3200, giving m = 246 and 0.67305298298962888...; interval-arithmetic acceptance is not a Lean proof, so hCert remains explicit. records.name: graham_pollak
records.doc: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Graham–Pollak theorem (1971) and its tightness on complete bipartite partitions of complete graphs. Proves that any partition of the edges of the complete graph K_n into m complete bipartite subgraphs requires at least n - 1 bipartite graphs (m >= n - 1), adapting Helge Tverberg's 1982 linear-algebraic quadratic form argument. Also formalizes the canonical star partition proving tightness. To the maintainers' knowledge, Graham–Pollak was not previously formalized in Mathlib (checked against Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: GrothendieckBessel.main
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the existence assertion in Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2608.12280v1 with the sharp constant K = 1: for every countable Bessel sequence with bound 1 in a complex Hilbert space, there exist measurable functions on the unit interval, pointwise bounded by 1, whose correlations reproduce the sequence's Gram matrix. This solves an open problem posed by Olevskii.

records.name: Palomar.main_theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22550: there is a family of lattice lines covering the integer plane whose set of realized directions is dense. Concretely, a family F of subsets of Z^2 is exhibited such that (i) every member is a genuine lattice line, the nonempty solution set of Px + Qy = c with P, Q coprime; (ii) the members cover Z^2; (iii) two members of different direction are disjoint, so no lattice point is covered twice in different directions; and (iv) the directions that occur are dense in the space RP^1 of line directions, that is, every angle in [0, pi) is approximated to within any epsilon by the direction of some member. The construction is recursive and works on nested regions: a chain of cosets Z^2 = R_0 > R_1 > R_2 > ... is built, and at stage k the region R_k is partitioned into sub-cosets of a new coprime direction, one of which is reserved to become R_{k+1} while lines of that direction claim all the others. Coverage is what the choice of reserved sub-coset is for: fix a surjective enumeration z_0, z_1, ... of Z^2 and reserve, at stage k, a sub-coset that does not contain z_k -- always possible, since the partition has at least four sub-cosets and only the one containing z_k must be avoided. Every point is then claimed: it is z_k for some k, and either it had already left the region at an earlier stage, in which case the coverage invariant Z^2 \ R_k = union over i < k of (R_i \ R_{i+1}) shows it was claimed there, or it is still in R_k and the reservation rule places it in a sub-coset claimed at stage k. Reserving an arbitrary sub-coset would not do: without that diagonal choice a point could survive in every R_k and never be claimed. Disjointness is a consequence of that partition rather than of any criterion for when two individual lines meet: distinct sub-cosets of a region are disjoint, each stage's lines stay inside the sub-cosets they claim, and the regions claimed at distinct stages are therefore disjoint. Earlier lines survive untouched because everything a later stage touches lies inside the reserved region. Only Theorem 1 is formalized; the paper's further remarks and discussion are not.

records.name: FsFormal.sdf_liminf_ge
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of an explicit construction for the Furstenberg-Sárközy problem. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1,...,N} with no nonzero square difference, the development proves that an explicit eleven-block constant alphaInf is at most liminf log D(N)/log N, that every exponent below alphaInf holds eventually pointwise, and that 0.7537 < alphaInf. The proof includes the finite certificates, the composite even-digit lift, CRT gluing, asymptotic passage, and kernel-checked numerical inequalities. This strictly improves Krachun's preceding explicit exponent 0.752796455874514... and moves the lower bound farther beyond 3/4.

records.name: BSCAveraging.MO285151.averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information
records.doc:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib development that settles three previously open problems about
binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source (DSBS): a pair (X, Y) of Bernoulli(1/2)
bits with P(X != Y) = p, together with Markov chains U - X - Y - V in which U and V are the
outputs of two independent binary channels applied to X and to Y. All quantities are in nats.

(1) MathOverflow 285151, "Do averaged binary symmetric channels maximize mutual information?"
(Georg Pichler, 2017; unanswered there) asks whether conv A = conv B, where A is the set of
rate triples (R0, R1, R2) with I(U;X) <= R1, I(Y;V) <= R2 and R0 <= I(U;V) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and B is the same set with both channels
restricted to be binary symmetric. The inclusion B subset A is elementary; the question is
whether taking convex hulls closes the gap, which the counterexample to the predecessor
question MathOverflow 213084 leaves open. This development proves conv A = conv B for every
p in [0,1] (`averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information`). The same statement settles
Conjecture 5.2 of Pichler, Piantanida and Matz, "Distributed Information-Theoretic
Clustering", Information and Inference 11 (2022) 1029-1082.

(2), (3) Conjectures 1 and 2 of Dikshtein, Ordentlich and Shamai (Shitz), "The Double-Sided
Information Bottleneck Function", Entropy 24(9):1321 (2022), which concern the double-sided
information bottleneck function R(Cu, Cv) = max I(U;V) subject to I(X;U) <= Cu and
I(Y;V) <= Cv at p = 0, that is X = Y. Conjecture 1 predicts that the maximising test channels
are a Z-channel and an S-channel; Conjecture 2 predicts that the pair maximising I(X;U,V) are
both Z-channels. Both are proved here for binary U and V, in optimality form: the Challenge
statements exhibit the conjectured channels themselves as `Chan` values and say that no
admissible pair beats them. No admissible pair exceeds the I(U;V) of the Z/S pair
(`conjecture1_p0_holds`), and none undercuts that of the Z/Z pair (`conjecture2_p0_holds`), at
every nondegenerate rate pair. A Z-channel and an S-channel are the same transition matrix up
to relabelling the input alphabet, so what the two conjectures distinguish is the relative
orientation of the two sides: anti-aligned for the maximum, aligned for the minimum.

The development is sorry-free and contains no hand-written axiom declaration.
`averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information` and `conjecture2_p0_holds` depend only on `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. `conjecture1_p0_holds` additionally depends on exactly one
further axiom: the 24129-monomial Polya certificate of its kernel lemma is checked by
`native_decide`, which on Lean v4.32.0 mints a per-declaration auxiliary axiom
(BSCAveraging.Reflect.kerQPE_allNonneg._native.native_decide.ax_1_1) rather than citing
`Lean.ofReduceBool`; that auxiliary axiom is a custom axiom in Comparator's sense. The other
computed step of that proof, a 650-cell interval sweep, is checked by the Lean kernel and adds
no axiom.

Scope, stated once for all three results. The channels are binary on both sides. For (1) this
is the setting of the source question. For (2) and (3) the reduction of the double-sided
bottleneck over arbitrary alphabets to binary test channels is Proposition 3 of the
Dikshtein-Ordentlich-Shamai paper and Proposition 4.3 of the Pichler-Piantanida-Matz paper; it
is cited here, not formalized, so read as statements about R(Cu, Cv, 0) with unrestricted
alphabets, (2) and (3) are conditional on that published cardinality bound. Conjecture 2 is
stated in its minimisation form, min I(U;V) at fixed rates; the identity
I(U;V) = I(U;X) + I(V;X) - I(X;U,V) that turns the paper's maximisation of I(X;U,V) into
that minimisation is the authors' own, given as Remark 5 of the same paper, and is likewise
not formalized here. Both
conjecture statements are value statements: they say the conjectured optimal value is not
beaten, not that the conjectured pair is the unique optimiser. p = 0 is the only case the
paper's Conjectures 1 and 2 state; Conjecture 3 of that paper, which concerns p above a
threshold, is not addressed.

Two endpoints of (1) were already settled in the literature and are reproved here rather than
established: p = 0, which Pichler-Piantanida-Matz note follows from their Corollary 4.1 and
Proposition 4.3, and the degenerate p = 1/2, where the two regions coincide without
convexification. The new content of (1) is p in (0,1/2) union (1/2,1). The binary restriction
costs nothing in (1): Conjecture 5.2 is stated for S_i, which is defined with the cardinality
bounds |U| <= |X| and |V| <= |Y|, and Proposition 4.3 of the same paper gives
conv(S_i) = conv(R_i).

Novelty has not been independently established. MathOverflow 285151 has no answer and no
comments (StackExchange API, asked 2017-11-03). The Dikshtein-Ordentlich-Shamai paper has one
recorded citing work, a 2024 Entropy editorial that mentions the setting but not the
conjectures, and no resolution of either conjecture was found. Mathlib at the pinned revision
contains no mutual information at all, and no prior Lean formalization of any of the three
problems was found. That search is the authors' own and is not offered as evidence of
priority.

records.name: bondy_induced_subsets
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of J. A. Bondy's 1972 theorem on induced subsets. Proves that for any family F of n distinct subsets of an arbitrary finite ground set X, there exists a distinguishing subset S ⊆ X of cardinality at most n - 1 such that the restriction map s ↦ s ∩ S is injective on F. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: bollobas_two_families
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Béla Bollobás's 1965 Two Families Theorem (Set Pairs Inequality) in extremal set theory. records.name: paper_c_theorem_one_two_i_deterministic_masks
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of three Poisson-limit statements for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function in a dyadic block, corresponding to the three clauses of Theorem 1.2 in the cited source article. The first proves a total-variation Poisson approximation uniformly over every deterministic mask of the dyadic block. The second gives the Laplace-functional characterization of the limiting spatial Poisson point process. The third gives the corresponding marked characterization together with uniform tightness of the discrete marks. All three compared statements are conditional on exactly three fully stated ordinary propositions specialized from Arratia--Goldstein--Gordon, Evertse--Silverman, and Nicolas--Robin. Those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

records.name: FriendshipTheorem.friendship_theorem
records.doc: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Friendship Theorem (P. Erdős, A. Rényi, and V. T. Sós, 1966; H. S. Wilf, 1971). Proves that any finite simple graph on at least three vertices (|V| ≥ 3) in which every pair of distinct vertices shares exactly one common neighbor must contain a universal vertex (the 'politician'), structuring the graph as a collection of triangles sharing a central vertex (a windmill graph). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: paper_c_theorem_one_four_moments
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of the first two moments and variance of the number of long constant-stretch starts of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function in a dyadic block, together with the quantitative exponential estimate for the separated homogeneous two-start sum. Uniformly in the critical window, Theorem 1.4 gives the first-moment rate, second falling-factorial-moment convergence, R_2(N,L)=o_C(N^2), and variance convergence; Corollary 11.3 gives the stronger bound R_2(N,L) <<_C N^2 exp(-c_R sqrt(log N)/log log N) for some c_R>0. Both compared statements are conditional on exactly two fully stated ordinary propositions specialized from Evertse--Silverman and Nicolas--Robin. Those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

records.name: SylvesterGallai.sylvester_gallai
records.doc:
A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Sylvester–Gallai theorem (J. J. Sylvester 1893, T. Gallai 1944, L. M. Kelly 1948; Freek Wiedijk #98). Proves that every finite non-collinear set of points in the real Euclidean plane contains an ordinary line passing through exactly two points of the set, formalized via Kelly's minimal point-line distance argument.

records.name: TemperedXi.F_differentiable
records.doc: This project formalizes in Lean 4 the zero geometry of the odd channel of Riemann's kernel, refuting conjectures of X.-J. Yang (Fractals 32 (2024) 2340116). Let Phi be the kernel of Riemann's integral representation, Phi(u) = sum_{n>=1} (4 pi^2 n^4 e^{9u/2} - 6 pi n^2 e^{5u/2}) e^{-pi n^2 e^{2u}}, the positive even function whose cosh transform is the completed zeta function, and let F(w) = 2 int_0^infty Phi(u) sinh(wu) du be the odd channel of the same kernel; this is Yang's "tempered xi function", in shifted coordinates. Six statements are compared: F is entire; F has infinitely many zeros; every nonzero zero of F has both real and imaginary parts nonzero; the zeros occur in quartets w, -w, conj w, -conj w; consequently the source paper's Conjecture 1, which asserts that every zero of the tempered xi function lies on the line Re s = 1/2, is false, and indeed apart from the origin no zero lies on that line; and the zeros of the sine channel t -> F(it) are not all real, which is the exactly formalizable content of the source paper's Conjecture 2. The audience is the study of real zeros of Fourier transforms of Riemann's kernel, the line of work of Lagarias and Montague (2011), Ki, Kim and Lee (2009), and the de Bruijn-Newman literature: the weight family interpolating the Lagarias-Montague integrated function and the odd xi derivatives places F at weight zero. Yang's conjectures are the occasion for the formalization, not its research context; Conjecture 1 was also the subject of a prize challenge publicly announced by its author, recorded here solely as evidence that the question was regarded as open and difficult, with no claim made concerning the prize itself. This entry makes no claim concerning the Riemann hypothesis. Scope limitation, stated plainly: the compared theorems quantify over the integral F as defined in the Challenge file. The classical identification of F with the odd part of the completed zeta function is NOT proved in Lean; it was checked numerically only (agreement to about forty digits at several complex points), and nothing in the formal development depends on it. On novelty: the refutation of the source conjectures is believed new. In the literature search completed 26 August 2026, every recorded citation of the source paper is a self-citation, the conjectures are restated as open in a 2026 invited review, and no refutation and no proof-assistant formalization of any compared statement was identified; that search is recorded but not exhaustive, and absence from search is not proof of open status. The component statements are not claimed as new: that F is entire of order one with infinitely many zeros was asserted, without proof, by Yang, Abdel-Aty and Geng (Thermal Science 27 (2023) 505-512) for this same function; the exclusion of zeros from the imaginary axis is, in sine-transform coordinates, a 1971 theorem of Spira, independently reproved here, with classical ancestry in Polya (1918, 1926) and Wintner (1935); and the quartet symmetry is recorded as a printed remark by Lagarias and Montague for the sibling weight family. The contribution recorded here is the proof-assistant formalization and its auditable dependency chain. As an aside: the supporting library pinned by this entry also contains a machine-checked counterexample, on the same axiom set, to a log-concavity conjecture of Coffey and Csordas for the derivatives of this same kernel; that theorem is not compared by this configuration and is mentioned only as context for the library.

records.name: CsordasCounterexample.J_nine_neg
records.doc: This project formalizes in Lean 4 a counterexample to a log-concavity conjecture of Coffey and Csordas (Math. Comp. 82 (2013) 2265-2272, Conjecture 2.5, where the quantity below is written S_n), later restated as Open Problem 4.13 of Csordas (Comput. Methods Funct. Theory 15 (2015) 373-391). Let Phi be the kernel of Riemann's integral representation, Phi(u) = sum_{n>=1} (4 pi^2 n^4 e^{9u/2} - 6 pi n^2 e^{5u/2}) e^{-pi n^2 e^{2u}}, and set J_n(t) = (Phi^(n)(t))^2 - Phi^(n-1)(t) Phi^(n+1)(t), the n-th Laguerre expression of Phi. The conjecture asserts J_n(t) > 0 for every real t and every n >= 1. The compared theorem proves J_9(0) < 0, refuting it. The mechanism is a single sign anomaly: Phi is even, so Phi^(9)(0) = 0 and J_9(0) = -Phi^(8)(0) Phi^(10)(0); the expected sign alternation of the even-order derivatives at the origin breaks at order ten, with Phi^(8)(0) and Phi^(10)(0) both positive. The formalization defines Phi through its convergent theta series, uses iterated derivatives, and derives evenness from Mathlib's Gaussian Poisson summation. The audience is the study of Laguerre expressions and Turan-type inequalities for the Riemann kernel: the Csordas school and its successors, who posed the conjecture and restated it as an open problem. The result is a counterexample, checkable directly by anyone with the definition of Phi in hand. This entry makes no claim concerning the Riemann hypothesis and no priority claim for the counterexample. Contemporaneous LLM-assisted exact-certificate proofs of the same sign failure are cited in the source metadata; neither is a proof-assistant formalization. The contribution recorded here is the Lean 4 formalization and its auditable dependency chain. As an aside: the supporting library pinned by this entry also contains machine-checked refutations, on the same axiom set, of conjectures of X.-J. Yang (Fractals 32 (2024) 2340116) asserting that the zeros of the tempered xi function -- the odd channel of this same kernel -- are confined to a single line; those theorems are not compared by this configuration and are mentioned only as context for the library.

records.name: FactorialHypergraph.Palomar.quantitative_auxiliary_erdos
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative solution to the auxiliary problem suggested by Erdos alongside Problem 1059. Conditional on an explicitly stated standard dimension-one upper-bound sieve theorem, the formalization proves that for every sufficiently large L there are at least ((L+1)!)^eta/(100 log L) integers n in (2L!, (L+1)!] whose prime factors all exceed L and for which n-k! is composite for every 1 <= k <= L. The formalization does not prove that n is prime and therefore does not solve the original Erdos prime problem.

records.name: FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graph_fundamental_group_free_rank
records.doc: Formalizes the fundamental group of a finite connected graph, represented as a finite weakly connected directed multigraph with its standard interval-cell quotient realization. The main result identifies the topological fundamental group at a chosen vertex with `FreeGroup (Fin (E + 1 - V))`. The proof compares the topological group with the endomorphism group at the root in Mathlib's free groupoid, whose explicit spanning-tree basis supplies the non-tree-edge generators. The development also proves the cycle-rank identities, root-change equivalences, the tree/triviality criterion, and the corresponding abelianization statement. It constructs a path-lifting quiver and verifies its covering property; the realization of that cover is proved contractible by an explicit quotient homotopy, and path lifting plus monodromy completes the comparison isomorphism.

records.name: NFNotWPP.NF_proves_not_WPP
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof that standard first-order New Foundations (NF), axiomatized by extensionality and the full stratified-comprehension schema, syntactically derives the negation of the Weak Partition Principle (WPP). The translated Metamath proof enters through eleven literal Hailperin sentences, which are used internally as a finite-basis bridge and are proved deductively equivalent to standard NF.

records.name: Kourovka1032.kourovka_10_32_conditional
records.doc: Answer to Problem 10.32 of the Kourovka Notebook, posed by Yu. I. Merzlyakov in 1986 and still open in the Notebook's 21st edition (2026), in both directions. Positive direction: there are constants C and N0 such that for all nonzero integers r, s with r or s odd, the word x^r y^s is universal on the symmetric group S_n (every permutation is a value) whenever n >= N0 and n >= C * log m(r,s), where m(r,s) is the product of the distinct primes dividing rs. This is the S_n analogue of the logarithmic Brenner-Evans-Silberger bound for A_n; the best previous S_n bound (Droste, 1986) was linear in m. The constant C is effective (the paper gives 4.65 for its fully effective cases), while the threshold N0 is ineffective solely because the proof uses Vinogradov's three-primes theorem. Negative direction, unconditional: the logarithmic shape is optimal. For r = lcm(1..n) with s its odd part, no element of order 3 in S_n is a value of x^r y^s, while log m(r,s) equals theta(n), the full Chebyshev mass of the primes up to n. The proof is machine-checked in Lean 4 on top of Mathlib, with the complete prose write-up included in this repository. The principal theorem, UniversalWords.kourovka_10_32_conditional, is a fully proved implication from eight explicitly stated published theorems (Herzog-Kaplan-Lev, Boccara, three Rosser-Schoenfeld bounds, Montgomery-Vaughan's Brun-Titchmarsh inequality, Vinogradov's three-primes theorem, and the Halberstam-Richert sieve bound) and depends only on Lean's three standard axioms, as does the optimality theorem UniversalWords.not_universal. A quarantined module assumes the eight statements as axioms to recover the unconditional form.

records.name: ColomboPalomar.odd_colombo_determinant_positive
records.doc: This project formalizes the odd-exponent branch of Colombo's determinant problem for even matrix size. For every m at least one, every strictly increasing x : Fin (2*m) → ℝ, and every r at least m - 1, it proves that the determinant of the matrix with entries (x_j - x_i)^(2*r+1) is strictly positive. The proof development passes through paired truncated-power determinants, B-spline and Marsden factorization, total nonnegativity, Volterra propagation, and Beta--de Bruijn and Pfaffian identities.

records.name: paper_c_theorem_sixteen_two_finite_cylinder
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of global and finite-prefix Poisson laws for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function, corresponding to Theorem 16.2 and Corollary 16.4 of the cited source article. The selected declarations give the global interior start-count law on a finite prime-sign cylinder, its recentering at M/2^L, the corresponding theorem on the infinite Rademacher product, and the finite-prefix start-count and longest-stretch law. All asymptotics are uniform in the critical window |L - log_2 M| <= C. Each declaration is conditional on exactly six fully stated ordinary source propositions; those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

records.name: SmallestOpenCubic.no_polynomial_family_deg_le_four
records.doc: This project formalizes in Lean 4 the statement that the Diophantine equation y*z*(y+z) = x^3 + x^2 + 3x - 1 admits no polynomial parametrization over the rationals whose x-coordinate has degree between 1 and 4. Writing f = X^3 + X^2 + 3X - 1, the compared theorem is that there is no triple of rational polynomials (g, u, v) with g nonconstant of degree at most 4 satisfying the identity u*v*(u+v) = f composed with g. Exhibiting such a family is one of the two standard ways an equation of this shape is settled affirmatively -- the other being a sporadic solution -- and the theorem closes that route at low degree. The statement is over the rationals, which is the stronger reading: an integer family is in particular a rational one, so the theorem also excludes integer families in the same degree range. The statement is unconditional and uses no hypothesis from the literature. Context, stated plainly and without overstatement: this equation is recorded on MathOverflow (question 509449, posed by Bogdan Grechuk) as the smallest cubic equation with open solvability problem under the size ordering H(P) = sum |a_i| 2^{d_i} used in that programme, at H = 35. The compared theorem does NOT decide whether the equation has integer solutions, and makes no claim to. A solution could still exist sporadically, or in a polynomial family whose x-coordinate has degree 5 or more, or the equation could be unsolvable for reasons this theorem does not touch. Degree 5 is not covered and is not claimed: it admits slot-degree shapes the argument for degree at most 4 does not reach, and the bound in the statement is exactly the bound that is proved. The audience is the programme that maintains and closes the frontier list this equation sits on -- Bogdan Grechuk and Ashleigh Ratcliffe, On the shortest open cubic equations (arXiv:2603.29831), and the MathOverflow thread 466803 that tracks the current smallest open equations -- together with the adjacent literature on cubic Diophantine equations of this shape: Janos Kollar and Jennifer Li on the Mordell-Schinzel conjecture for cubic Diophantine equations XYZ = G(X,Y) (arXiv:2412.12080), and Martin Bright and Julian Lyczak on log K3 surfaces (arXiv:1705.04529), whose setting -- a del Pezzo surface minus a smooth anticanonical divisor -- is the geometry of the affine surface defined by this equation. Ruling out low-degree parametric families is directly responsive to how equations on that frontier list are resolved. On novelty: a literature search recorded 2026-07-21 and repeated 2026-08-26 identified no indexed resolution of the equation and no proof-assistant formalization touching it or the frontier list; the search is recorded but not exhaustive, and absence from search is not proof of open status. That search establishes that the equation is open; it does NOT establish that the non-existence of low-degree polynomial families is a new observation, and no such claim is made here. The contribution recorded by this entry is the proof-assistant formalization and its auditable dependency chain.

records.name: RG_eq_DFA
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of grammar and automaton presentations of the extended Chomsky hierarchy. Starting from unrestricted-grammar rewriting, it defines regular, linear, context-free, context-sensitive, indexed, deterministic context-free, recursive, and recursively enumerable language classes; relates finite, pushdown, linearly bounded, and Mathlib TM0 automata to the corresponding grammar classes; proves strict hierarchy inclusions; and establishes closure or non-closure under thirteen operations for seven major classes.

Starting from unrestricted-grammar rewriting, it defines regular, linear, context-free, context-sensitive, indexed, deterministic context-free, recursive, and recursively enumerable language classes; relates finite, pushdown, linearly bounded, and Mathlib TM0 automata to the corresponding grammar classes; proves strict hierarchy inclusions; and establishes closure or non-closure under thirteen operations for seven major classes.

Starting from unrestricted-grammar rewriting, it defines regular, linear, context-free, context-sensitive, indexed, deterministic context-free, recursive, and recursively enumerable language classes; relates finite, pushdown, linearly bounded, and Mathlib TM0 automata to the corresponding grammar classes; proves strict hierarchy inclusions; and establishes closure or non-closure under thirteen operations for seven major classes.

records.name: HallMarriage.hall_marriage_theorem
records.doc:
A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Hall's Marriage Theorem (Philip Hall 1935, Halmos–Vaughan 1950; Freek Wiedijk #87). Proves that an indexed family of finite sets admits a system of distinct representatives (SDR) if and only if Hall's marriage condition holds.
To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name,
    docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: JacobianCounterexample.jacobianDet_F
records.doc: An independent Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the explicit three-dimensional polynomial map announced by Levent Alpöge in 2026. The project proves that its formal Jacobian determinant is the nonzero constant -2, verifies an explicit three-point fibre over the complex numbers, and derives the failure of injectivity required to refute the dimension-three Jacobian conjecture. The source formulas and proof scope are recorded explicitly; no claim is made about the still-open two-dimensional case.

records.name: SpernerND.sperner_nd_parity
records.doc: A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the general n-dimensional combinatorial Sperner parity theorem on abstract n-dimensional pseudomanifolds with boundary for arbitrary dimension n : ℕ. Proves the local door-counting parity invariant on (n+1)-simplices, the global double-counting identity on door-facet incidences, and the master parity congruence modulo 2 relating panchromatic (n+1)-simplices to boundary doors. The theorem is conditional on an odd number of boundary (n-1)-doors; obtaining the classical geometric Sperner lemma for simplicial subdivisions of geometric simplices with boundary-preserving colorings is a specialization requiring an additional geometric boundary induction argument not contained in these abstract combinatorial declarations. This n-dimensional development (SpernerND.lean) generalizes and supersedes the fixed-dimensional combinatorial parity identities in the repository's lower-dimensional modules (SpernersLemma.lean and Sperner3D.lean) into a single unified parameterized architecture. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: HigherLambdaModel.Palomar.main_result
records.doc: A Lean formalization of higher-dimensional structure in the untyped lambda calculus.  Arthur Ramos is the first author and responsible maintainer of the Lean formalization; Daniel O. Martinez-Rivillas and Ruy J.G.B. de Queiroz are credited as the mathematical/source authors whose results are formalized.  The Palomar surface uses a restricted Kan-complex exponential and a separate certificate for term-generated semantic bodies, while the substantive repository also formalizes the higher conversion tower and the concrete K-infinity homotopy lambda model.

records.name: descartes_rule_of_signs
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Descartes's Rule of Signs (1637, Wiedijk #73). Proves that for any non-zero real polynomial p(X) over ℝ, the number of positive real roots counted with algebraic multiplicity is bounded above by the number of sign variations in its coefficient sequence (ignoring zero coefficients), and their difference is an even non-negative integer. While the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1) contains the upper-bound inequality in `Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.RuleOfSigns` (`Polynomial.roots_countP_pos_le_signVariations`), this development formalizes the complete two-part theorem by proving the even-parity conclusion (Gauss 1828), establishing the sign-variation parity correspondence with leading and trailing coefficients, and providing a direct list-based coefficient sequence interface.

records.name: Palomar.splitLevi_mem_spin_isometry_range_iff_det_square
records.doc: Formalizes an exterior-model spinor construction for a field K in which 2 is invertible, using an explicit hyperbolic presentation and the Clifford conjugation action on the ambient quadratic space.  The development proves field-sensitive covering and image results: the positive split-rank spin-to-isometry kernel is {1,-1}, the spin action therefore descends only projectively, the split-line image is exactly the square-scaling subgroup, and a finite-dimensional split Levi element associated to g lies in the ambient spin image exactly when det(g) is a square unit.  The repository also packages the chosen exterior model, half-spin pieces, explicit transvection and square-scaling Clifford lifts, square-class quotient characters, vector-product norm identities, and selected complex and real low-dimensional Clifford classifications.

records.name: CollatzEndpointTransportPalomar.quantitative_arbitrary_target_endpoint_transport
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative stability theorem for the one-block endpoint-pullback operator of the shortcut Collatz map. If an arbitrary target set has at most C N^(1-D) exceptions among the positive integers up to N, then, for every central Renyi order 1/2 < theta < 1, every admissible fixed central window, and every positive transport coefficient below the explicit asymptotic slope, its pullback through one floor(log_2 n)-step endpoint is (K(C+1)D^(-(1+theta)), transport*D)-dense whenever D is sufficiently small. The cutoff and K depend only on the fixed moment and transport parameters, not on the target set or C,D. This is an operator-level arbitrary-target theorem, not a pointwise convergence or eventual-descent claim.

records.name: SunCotangentP29.cotangentPermanent29_exact
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the exact evaluation of the normalized 14 by 14 cotangent permanent at p = 29. The formalization proves that its value is 84643985981440 and hence gives a counterexample to the cotangent sign inequality in Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture 4.7(ii). It includes the analytic-to-cyclotomic bridge, two separately kernel-checked finite permanent certificates, Chinese-remainder and coefficientwise integer lifting, the Section 3 Archimedean uniqueness argument, and equation (4.1) in the integral cyclotomic quotient.

records.name: SchwarzschildVacuum.einstein_eq_zero_iff_ricciFlat
records.doc: Twenty-one theorems and thirty-three definitions, machine-checked in Lean 4 against Mathlib v4.32.0: the Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Kottler), Reissner-Nordstrom (with the Maxwell stress tensor defined and G = 8 pi T proved in all sixteen components), ingoing Vaidya (null dust of rank at most one, rank one wherever dm/dv ≠ 0, for a merely once-differentiable mass function), spatially flat FLRW (both Friedmann equations in Einstein-tensor form), static de Sitter, Minkowski-in-spherical and Kiselev metrics, together with Birkhoff uniqueness in the areal static gauge and the n != 2 equivalence of the two forms of the vacuum equations. The results are classical and NO NEW MATHEMATICS IS CLAIMED: this is a proof of concept for the definitions. Lean checks that a proof establishes a statement, not that a definition means what its name says, so the entry certifies its sign, index and contraction conventions by computing textbook solutions with them -- including four NONZERO answers (de Sitter R = 12/L^2, Reissner-Nordstrom R_thetatheta = Q^2/r^2, Vaidya R_vv = 2 (dm/dv)/r^2, Kiselev R_thetatheta = -3wc r^-(3w+1)), because a curvature definition that was accidentally identically zero would still prove every vacuum theorem here. Scope: everything is a computation in ONE FIXED CHART, an open subset of R^4 -- no atlas, no manifold, no coordinate-independence theorem, no maximal extension, and horizons and coordinate poles lie outside every statement. NOT compared: Ricci symmetry R_bd = R_db in general (it needs Clairaut for the coordinate partial derivative, which Mathlib supplies only for fderiv) or the Bianchi identities; Maxwell's own equations; any matter model, fluid or energy condition beyond the single defined Maxwell stress tensor; non-flat FLRW; the outgoing Vaidya chart. Audience: general relativists, for whom this is the definitional layer a junction-condition or thin-shell statement would be written against, and the formalization community, for whom it is coverage-creating rather than coverage-duplicating. Mathlib v4.32.0 contains no curvature of any kind -- christoffel, ricci, scalarCurvature, Lorentzian, PseudoRiemannian and five further names return zero hits across all 8,264 .lean files at the pinned revision, and its one metric structure hard-codes positive definiteness -- so the entire chain is defined inline in the Challenge.

records.name: GCD369PolynomialCubeSourceExclusion
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the source-facing polynomial-cube exclusion at actual partial degrees (6,9).  From literal bivariate polynomials of outer degrees six and nine, leading coefficients s^6 and s^9 for a common polynomial s, and nonzero constant Keller bracket, the formalization proves that no such source exists, including when s is constant.  It constructs the finite-pole or infinity expansion, exhausts every timing of the eight Faber loads through rho2, and excludes the remaining elliptic, cusp, zero-invariant, and constant-core terminal fibres.  It does not claim the reduction from an arbitrary Keller pair, all (6,9), maximum eleven, or the plane Jacobian conjecture.

records.name: DinitzGargGoemans.allSourceTerminalPaths
records.doc: A standalone Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the finite counterexample to the cost-preserving single-source unsplittable-flow conjecture. The development realizes a directed graph with seven vertices, nine arcs, and three terminal demands; checks a feasible rational fractional flow of cost 58 with maximum demand 15; and proves that every unsplittable routing under the weak additive congestion bound has cost at least 60. It also derives the failure of the strict congestion variant. No general algorithmic or complexity-theoretic claim is made.

records.name: TwoCertificatePalomar.two_certificate_supporting_plane

records.name: TopologicalComputationalPaths.main_result
records.doc: A Lean formalization of topological semantics for endpoint-varying computational paths.  It constructs both the canonical final composable quotient and the ordinary pullback of quotient arrows.  The selected result proves that the canonical comparison is a continuous bijection and characterizes exactly when it is quotient, a homeomorphism, and an induced topology agreement; under these equivalent conditions ordinary composition is continuous.  It also records discontinuity as an obstruction and proves compact--Hausdorff and discrete sufficient cases.  The selected certificate additionally requires full additive classifications of the genuine based-loop spaces `AddCircle (1 : ℝ)` by `ℤ` and its product torus by `ℤ × ℤ`: the invariant, identity value, composition additivity, explicit standard representatives, and both inverse laws are checked using covering-map lifts and coordinatewise arguments.  It also formalizes the observable based fiber of the universal continuous-path presentation, its homeomorphism to the standard based loop quotient, the final/ordinary pair comparison, and the source-backed Hawaiian-earring transfer: the non-quotient square and discontinuous multiplication force failure of the scoped ordinary-pair quotient, topology agreement, and ordinary multiplication continuity under the comparison.

records.name: Palomar.beyond_bethe_permanent
records.doc: Computing or approximating the permanent is a canonical problem in theoretical computer science and in counting and sampling.  Before this work, the canonical Bethe approximation gave the best known deterministic guarantee, with approximation factor (sqrt 2)^n.  This formalization proves that there is an absolute constant c < sqrt 2 and a deterministic polynomial-time c^n-approximation for every nonnegative rational matrix. It checks the mathematical and algorithmic proof down to Lean's standard logical axioms, including the finite-precision convex-optimization implementation.

records.name: RadonHelly.radons_theorem
records.doc: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Radon's Lemma (Johann Radon, 1921) and Helly's Theorem on intersecting families of convex sets (Eduard Helly, 1923; Freek Wiedijk #99) from first principles. Proves that any d + 2 points in ℝ^d admit a Radon partition into two disjoint subsets whose convex hulls intersect, and uses Radon's lemma by induction on the family size to prove Helly's theorem for finite families of convex sets under the general <= d + 1 subfamily intersection hypothesis (covering small families |ι| <= d + 1 as well as large families). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: ColorfulCaratheodory.colorful_caratheodory_point
records.doc: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Bárány's Colorful Carathéodory Theorem (1982), Bárány's First Selection Lemma (1982), the 1D Centerpoint Theorem, and geometric deductions from first principles. Proves that for any d + 1 sets of points S_0, ..., S_d in R^d whose convex hulls all contain a common target point p, there exists a colorful transversal f (selecting f(i) in S_i for each color class i) whose convex hull conv({f(0), ..., f(d)}) contains p. Formulated over arbitrary dimension d, with specializations to the origin and low dimensions (d = 0, 1, 2), a formal deduction of the classical Carathéodory theorem bound, the 1D Centerpoint Theorem (median contains >= floor((n+1)/2) = ceil(n/2) points in each half-line), Bárány's 1982 First Selection Lemma (>= (|P|/2)(|P|-|P|/2) pairs containing the centerpoint), and the 1D Colorful Selection Lemma (at least one colorful pair covering p). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: erdos_szekeres_convex_polygon
records.doc: A comprehensive, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Erdős–Szekeres Convex Polygon Theorem (1935). Formalizes orientation determinants, general position, 2D rotation transformations with finite slope avoidance (rotating any finite set to have mutually distinct x-coordinates), x-coordinate sorting, cup-cap sequences with Pascal-type binomial split recurrences, halfspace separation for convex hulls, and rotation invariance of convex polygons. Proves that any finite set of at least choose(2k - 4, k - 2) + 1 points in general position in ℝ² contains the vertices of a strictly convex k-gon, verifying the Happy Ending Theorem under pure general position with no distinct-x-coordinate restriction. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: PalomarHS.main_result
records.doc: A kernel-checked Lean formalization of the exact no-broken-circuit volume identity for hard-sphere Mayer cluster integrals and the stronger dimension-three fork-packing upper bound for each tree-owned NBC region. The development proves finite broken-circuit cancellation, the measurable finite-region decomposition, the anchored Euclidean product-measure theorem, and its explicit flat-coordinate transport.  Its geometric result is the attachment-aware estimate Vol(NBC_T) <= (17/32)^hardSphereNu T * hardSphereKappa^(k-1), where hardSphereNu T is the maximum cardinality of a packing of pairwise vertex-disjoint, order-compatible forks in T.  A formal fork is an ordered triple (a,b,c) with a < b < c, center a, leaves b,c, and tree edges {a,b} and {a,c}.  The central contribution is the complete pointwise-to-integral bridge together with the orientation-aware measure-preserving factorization that realizes the per-fork volume suppression.

records.name: PrimeStar.palomar_uniform_finite_prime_sum
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the ordered adjacency spectrum of finite prime-cover graphs. Its root-centred specialization proves that the square of the largest ordered eigenvalue equals pi(X) plus four times the finite prime sum of 1/(p-1), up to o(1). More generally, for every fixed finite set S of deleted primes and epsilon > 0, the same law with the explicit centre correction c(a) holds uniformly over allowed centres a <= (log X)^(1/2-epsilon). The same window admits a uniform centre--shell evolution theorem at the explicit first-exit frequency, with a finite localization-plus-phase error bound.

records.name: PrimeStar.palomar_top_finite_prime_sum
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the ordered adjacency spectrum of finite prime-cover graphs. Its root-centred specialization proves that the square of the largest ordered eigenvalue equals pi(X) plus four times the finite prime sum of 1/(p-1), up to o(1). More generally, for every fixed finite set S of deleted primes and epsilon > 0, the same law with the explicit centre correction c(a) holds uniformly over allowed centres a <= (log X)^(1/2-epsilon). The same window admits a uniform centre--shell evolution theorem at the explicit first-exit frequency, with a finite localization-plus-phase error bound.

records.name: HurwitzClassification.hurwitz_classification
records.doc: Hurwitz's theorem (1898), classification form: a nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean composition algebra over R - a unital, not necessarily associative or commutative bilinear product together with a symmetric positive-definite form whose quadratic form is multiplicative - is isomorphic to R, C, the quaternions or the octonions, by a linear isomorphism preserving the unit, the product and the norm form. All four targets are constructed, with Degen's eight-square identity discharging the octonion composition law, so every branch of the conclusion is attained. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

records.name: PalomarFeige.sharp_unit_slack_feige_complete
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the sharp unit-slack (delta = 1) small-deviation inequality for sums of independent nonnegative random variables. For every positive integer n and every independent family X_1, ..., X_n of measurable, integrable, nonnegative random variables satisfying E[X_i] <= 1, writing S = sum_i X_i, it proves the sharp bound P(S < E[S] + 1) >= (n / (n + 1))^n and proves that this constant is optimal for each fixed n. This optimal dimension-dependent bound strengthens and implies Feige's 1/e conjecture. The repository also formalizes the Vlassis-Thomas exact calibration theorem and Grünbaum's centroid-halfspace inequality used in the proof.

records.name: HadamardFormal.handshake_mod_four
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the periodic Cooper-Wallis construction and of Hadamard existence at eight orders: from kernel-checked periodic T-matrix quadruples of orders 103 and 163 and seven symmetric-circulant Williamson quadruples, the development proves that Hadamard matrices of orders 2884, 4532, 7004, 7172, 7828, 8476, 9476, and 11948 exist. Each of the eight orders lands on an entry of Table 4 of Cati and Pasechnik's maintained construction database (arXiv:2411.18897v2, 2025-08-30) recording no Hadamard matrix of that order as known, and the source repositories' firsthand audit of the construction literature (closed 2026-08-29) located no published route to the order-103 or order-163 T-objects the eight are built from. The development also proves the erratum core of the companion Hadamard-M note on Miyamoto's 1991 construction paper: the handshake parity obstruction, its empty-class corollary, and the nonexistence of the displayed C2-matrix ingredient of that paper's Corollary 4 at every positive block order not congruent to 1 mod 4 - covering the paper's printed list entries at orders 103, 127, and 151 under both printed readings of the corollary's output order, and leaving the order-515 list entry, the paper's claim of a Hadamard matrix of order 2060, unsupported by the paper's own machinery. Cati and Pasechnik, for want of details, record being unable to verify the constructions claimed in that paper's section 7, naming order 4*515 as their example; the obstruction supplies an independent mathematical reason the printed route cannot deliver that entry. Order 2060 itself is not open: a Hadamard matrix of that order was posted publicly on 2026-08-23, credited to Schneider, by other means.

records.name: GraphCoveringTheory.schreier_index_formula
records.doc: Formalizes the sharp Schreier index formula for a finite-index subgroup of a free group on a finite nonempty generating type. For a finite nonempty type alpha, a subgroup H of FreeGroup alpha with finite index d is proved equivalent, as a group, to FreeGroup (Fin (1 + d * (card alpha - 1))). More strongly, the repository exposes a FreeGroupBasis for H with this indexing type. The proof realizes H as the vertex group of the finite action-groupoid covering on the coset space, verifies the covering locally by explicit star and costar bijections, and counts the complement of a geodesic spanning tree. It also exposes the truncation-safe natural-number statement and the generic finite free-groupoid rank calculation used by the submission theorem. For finite-index normal subgroups, a companion module proves that every deck transformation of the finite Schreier action is a unique right translation by the quotient group.

records.name: frankl_wilson_uniform
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Frankl–Wilson theorem (1981) for modulo-p intersecting set families. Uses the polynomial linear algebra method over ZMod p to prove both the general non-uniform bound |F| <= sum_{i=0}^s choose(n, i) and the uniform cardinality bound |F| <= choose(n, s). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: MahlerWindow.quadratic_min
records.doc: For each degree d in {2, 3, 4}, the polynomial x^d - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer polynomials of degree d with Mahler measure above one, and the three minimal values are exactly the golden ratio (M^2 = M + 1), the plastic ratio (M^3 = M + 1), and the root of x^4 - x^3 - 1 above one (M^4 = M^3 + 1); by Siegel's classical theorem (1944, cited as background, not formalized here) the latter two are the smallest and second-smallest Pisot numbers. Classically the degree-4 minimizer is not itself a Pisot polynomial, yet its measure lands back on the Pisot list via the reciprocal transform. The minimizers' irreducibility is part of the compared surface. Proofs are by a Graeffe-certificate architecture: an effective coefficient-bound box from Mathlib's norm_coeff_le_choose_mul_mahlerMeasure, then one integer certificate per box element (tie orbit, cyclotomic cofactor, explicit factorization, or an iterated Graeffe coefficient bound), 6,171 + 147 + 21 certificates kernel-decided with plain decide — no native_decide anywhere. The exact values follow from a root-inversion identity and a (sigma, s)-reduction localizing the conjugate pairs, with multiplicity excluded by kernel-certified measure brackets.

records.name: HumanVerification.equalAreaEqualPerimeterPartition
records.doc: Formalization of the result by A. Akopyan, S. Avvakumov, and R. Karasev that every convex figure in the plane can be partitioned into n convex pieces having equal area and equal perimeter for any n≥1.

records.name: ColorfulHelly.colorful_helly
records.doc: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Lovász's Colorful Helly Theorem (1974 / Bárány 1982). Proves that for any d + 1 finite families of convex sets in R^d such that every colorful transversal has a non-empty intersection, at least one entire family has a non-empty intersection. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.name: MeasurableSelection.exists_measurable_selection
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem: for an arbitrary measurable space (alpha, A) and a Polish space Y, a multifunction Phi : alpha -> Set Y with nonempty closed values that is weakly measurable (the hit set {a | Phi a meets U} lies in A for every open U) admits an A-to-Borel measurable selection f with f a in Phi a for every a.  The statement is measure-free and pointwise: no measure appears, and the selection property holds everywhere, not almost everywhere.  It is proved from Mathlib alone, by the classical argument — a dense sequence in Y, a recursion producing measurable countably-valued approximate selectors whose successive stages stay within (1/2)^n, and a uniform Cauchy limit that is measurable as a pointwise limit of measurable functions and lands in Phi a because Phi a is closed.  The measurability of each refinement step is obtained by splitting over the countably many measurable fibres of the previous stage's index function, on each of which the test set is cut out by a fixed open set, so the weak measurability hypothesis applies directly.  No measurable selection theorem exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas–Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Jankov–von Neumann uniformization, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  The measurable selection theorem is used in that development to produce plain-Borel-measurable feasible bicausal strategies.
